summary: The DNESKAi photo kit is three files in quorum/studio (dneskai-slide.ts 434 lines, dneskai-photo.ts 329, dneskai-layout.ts 480) on top of the shared carousel engine. renderDneskaiSlide picks one of 14 template ids by slide type (8 compositions; sources-0..6 is one layout by thumbnail count; statement has an INK variant), fits text by stepping 1 px from max to min size with Czech ties, lays the slide out for its content, and renders through the same renderer and gates as every other venture: 4.5:1 WCAG and APCA Lc 40 on every ground (photographs measured against their extremes under the cover shade), logo clear space and minimum height from the kit manifest. The kit is hardcoded twice (CAROUSEL_BRANDS['caught-up'] at :359 and :417), templates resolve by literal id and the layout re-flow dispatches on literal ids (:150-160) with CAP_OFFSET 0.3 tuned to the three caught-up faces. The accepted kit-engine ADR (looks over the brand kit, flows in the kit) is being implemented on fable/dneskai-kits. Two facts change the consolidation math: the dneskai-slide import closure is 30 of 52 source files and 14,893 of 17,921 lines (because CAROUSEL_BRANDS lives in library.ts, which imports every deck family, recipes and summaries), so 'fork only the DNESKAi kit' is not small; and 95 Quorum files outside studio/ import the package, but only one test touches the DNESKAi API. Smaller findings: the font-metric charset leaves out U+201A although all three faces carry it, so Czech inner quotes are refused downstream; there is no DNESKAi specimen sheet and the golden pins 11 hashes covering 8 of 14 templates; photographs are decoded twice per slide (validate and render).

findings.title: The font-metric charset leaves out U+201A, so Czech inner quotes ‚…‘ are refused although every face carries the glyph
findings.claim: generate-font-metrics.ts measures a fixed set (Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Cyrillic and 15 extras) that includes „ “ ‘ ’ but not ‚ (U+201A). hasCommittedGlyph reads only those tables, so OwnDashboard's glyph gate refuses any field containing ‚ with unsupported-glyph, although the cmaps of Space Grotesk, Source Serif 4 and IBM Plex Mono contain it.
findings.recommendation: Add ‚ (and ‛ if wanted) to the extras, run `pnpm -C studio fonts:metrics`, check golden, re-vendor. Add a test that every Czech typographic character in a fixed list is in each kit face's table.
findings.impactStatement: A correct Czech quotation inside a quotation (‚takto‘) makes the whole deck refused and costs a paid retry or an owner edit. Rare in headlines, but quotes are a core statement-slide device.

truth.evidence: Code confirmed: generate-font-metrics.ts:153 has no U+201A, fonts.ts:160-161 checks only the tables, dneskai-render.ts:159 refuses. The cmap probe shows all three DNESKAi faces carry U+201A. But generation already steers around it: dneskai-generation.ts:122 tells the model 'Never nest quotations and never use the low single quote ‚ or ‘ as a quotation mark; rephrase instead.' So only an owner edit can hit the refusal.

correctedLocations.excerpt: Never nest quotations and never use the low single quote ‚ or ‘ as a quotation mark; rephrase instead.

impact.reason: The prompt already avoids the character and owner edits with nested Czech quotes are rare; fold the one-line charset fix into the next metrics regeneration on the kits branch.

findings.title: The DNESKAi kit is hardcoded in four places, so five kits need engine changes, not data

A kit cannot be added by a manifest or token file alone.

findings.recommendation: Implement ADR-final as planned on fable/dneskai-kits (looks over the kit, flows declared per kit, cap height as metric data, kit input on DneskaiSlideInput), keeping the editorial kit byte-identical (11 golden hashes).
findings.impactStatement: Blocks owner goal 3 (five switchable kits) until the engine change lands; every kit that changes compositions, not only tokens, needs layout code.

truth.evidence: dneskai-slide.ts:359 and :417 pass CAROUSEL_BRANDS['caught-up']; :193-200 resolve by literal id; dneskai-layout.ts:150-160 dispatch on ids; :92 CAP_OFFSET constant with :86-91 naming the three faces. ADR-final section 3 lists the same constraints; the kits branch has started removing them but main is unchanged.

impact.reason: This is the engine work five kits depend on; it is already designed and under way, so the owner needs to see it as the critical path.

findings.title: 'Fork only the DNESKAi kit' is not small: the dneskai-slide import closure is 83 % of the studio
findings.claim: dneskai-slide.ts imports CAROUSEL_BRANDS from library.ts, which imports families, designs and recipes, so its closure is 30 of 52 source files and 14,893 of 17,921 lines. On the Quorum side, 95 files import the package but only orchestrator/tests/studio-lifecycle.test.ts uses the DNESKAi API. Option (b) copies a 18k-line engine that Quorum keeps changing for other ventures; option (c) needs CAROUSEL_BRANDS split out of library.ts first.
findings.recommendation: Before choosing (b) or (c), make the DNESKAi closure small in Quorum: move CAROUSEL_BRANDS (or the caught-up tokens) into a leaf module so dneskai-slide no longer pulls families/recipes/summary; re-measure the closure; then decide. Recommend (a) until the kit engine lands, then (c) on the reduced closure.
findings.impactStatement: Sets the real effort of the consolidation decision: (a) keep upstream = M per design change (rendering REN-02); (b) whole-studio copy = L once plus permanent divergence; (c) DNESKAi-only fork = M to cut the closure (move brand tokens out of library.ts) plus L to copy renderer/validation/text/fonts, after which OwnDashboard owns about 9-10k lines and the gates that protect them.

truth.evidence: dneskai-slide.ts:6 imports CAROUSEL_BRANDS from library.ts; library.ts:14-16 import families, designs and recipe. Closure measured by script: 30 files, 14,893 lines, including summary.ts and every families-*.ts. 95 Quorum files import the package; the only DNESKAi API use outside studio/ is orchestrator/tests/studio-lifecycle.test.ts:33. Effort figures per option are estimates.

impact.ownerDecision: Consolidation option (a) / (b) / (c), and whether to first move brand tokens out of library.ts in Quorum.
impact.reason: Changes the consolidation recommendation from 'fork the kit, it is small' to 'shrink the closure first'; the owner decides with real numbers.

findings.title: The studio has two looser notions of 'fits' than OwnDashboard enforces
findings.claim: The studio reports text-clipped as non-blocking and renders the cut slide, and it never reports a character a field's face lacks, because resvg gets all 46 faces and falls back silently. OwnDashboard compensates with its own blocking rules and a glyph gate, so the truth about a slide lives in two repositories.

evidence.excerpt: clipped.push(problem("text-clipped", false, field, `The ${field} does not fit ${fit.slot} whole and would be cut; shorten it.`));
const font = { loadSystemFonts: false, fontFiles: fontFiles(), defaultFontFamily: "IBM Plex Sans" };

findings.recommendation: Add an option (or a DNESKAi default) for inspect() to report missing glyphs per field face and to make clipping blocking; then drop the duplicate check in OwnDashboard as UPSTREAM.md already plans.
findings.impactStatement: Any new consumer (a Design Lab preview, a specimen script) that calls the studio directly would show cut or wrong-face text as fine. Matters most once kits multiply the faces.

truth.evidence: dneskai-slide.ts:364 blocking false; renderer.ts:605 hands all faces to resvg; UPSTREAM.md:58-62 documents the OwnDashboard compensation and the plan to drop it.

impact.reason: OwnDashboard's gate already covers it, and REN-09 keeps any Design Lab preview on that gate; worth doing in Quorum later, not an owner item.

findings.title: Photographs are decoded twice per slide, once to validate and once to render
findings.claim: inspect() reads metadata and decodes every photograph to PNG (rotate().png()); validateDneskaiSlide and renderDneskaiSlide each call inspect(), and OwnDashboard validates the deck during generation before the job renders it. Photo slides take 58-236 ms warm against 31-52 ms for a text slide.

evidence.excerpt: const { data, info } = await sharp(bytes, { limitInputPixels: DNESKAI_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS }).rotate().png().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
const { problems, template, payload, images } = await inspect(input);

findings.recommendation: Cache decoded PNG and size per asset sha256 in a small in-process LRU inside the studio; the bytes are content-addressed, so the cache cannot go stale.
findings.impactStatement: Small today (well under a second per deck); with five kits validated and rendered it is 10 decodes per photo per post. Worth fixing only alongside kit work.

truth.evidence: dneskai-slide.ts:323 metadata and :330 full decode inside inspect(); :404 and :409 both call inspect(); images.ts keeps only a crop WeakMap (:130), no decode cache. own-dashboard generation.ts:266 validates before the job renders.

impact.reason: Sub-second today; only matters if five kits are validated and rendered per post, which the cost model can revisit.

findings.title: Contrast, safe-area and logo gates run on every render; a new kit's palette is checked automatically
findings.claim: renderSlides runs validateTemplateForBrand on every ground before drawing: WCAG 4.5:1 and APCA Lc 40 per text/ground pair, photographs measured at their extremes under the shade, safe area, overflow; the logo is sized from the kit's clear space and minimum height. A look whose palette fails throws instead of rendering.

evidence.excerpt: const failed = validateTemplateForBrand(template, onGround, input.format).filter((check) => check.status === "fail");

findings.recommendation: Keep the gates in the critical path of every kit; add the kits to the gate tests (one render per kit and template) rather than writing new contrast code.
findings.impactStatement: The brand's '4.5:1 against every ground' rule and logo clear space are already enforced in code; five kits inherit that for free. Any port or fork must keep these gates.

truth.evidence: renderer.ts:474-493 checks every ground before drawing and throws on any failed check; validation.ts:164 and :225-226 contrast and APCA; contrast-apca.ts:116; renderer.ts:297-298 logo sizing. grounds.ts:87-105 measures photographs at both extremes for carousel-template/2, which every DNESKAi template is (dneskai-photo.ts:144).

impact.reason: Tells the owner that contrast and logo rules are already machine-enforced, and that kit tests should reuse them; cheap to extend.
